question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{4}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{-{x}^{7}+3}{{x}^{4}+6x+2} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{-{x}^{7}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{6x}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(-{x}^{3}+\frac{3}{{x}^{4}})}{(1+\frac{6}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\text{ }\frac{-{x}^{3}+0}{1+0+0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,-{x}^{3} \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
